> [!abstract] Key idea
> This tag uses **nested square rings**: each ring is one resonator and one bit. Four mirrored groups make the tag symmetric, so its code reads the same at both polarizations.

- The tag looks like an FSS on a thin grounded substrate.
- Five rings per group give a **5-bit tag**.
- It uses the same **Monostatic RCS** setup as [[8. Chipless RFID Fundamentals|Section 8]], from 2 to 9 GHz.

## 0.2 Building the Rings
- Each ring is a brick minus a smaller brick, drawn in one quadrant.
- Because width and gap are both W, every coordinate is a **multiple of W**.

| Ring k | Outer brick runs from | Inner brick runs from |
|---|---|---|
| **Formula** | (2k - 1)W to L/2 - (2k - 1)W | 2kW to L/2 - 2kW |
| **Ring 1** | W to L/2 - W | 2W to L/2 - 2W |
| **Ring 2** | 3W to L/2 - 3W | 4W to L/2 - 4W |

- After drawing one ring, copy its expression and change only the multiplier.
- **Mirror Copy** along X, then along Y, gives all four groups.

## 0.3 Simulation
- Place the field probe at Z = 50, outside the simulation box.
- Set the solver **accuracy to -80 dB** in Setup Solver.
- The RCS plot shows **five notches**, one for each ring size.

> [!info] Why tighten the accuracy
> The Time Domain solver stops once the energy has decayed to the accuracy level. Resonant tags hold energy for a long time, so a stricter level gives accurate notches.

> [!tip] Sanity check on the ring sizes
> Using the same perimeter rule as Section 8, ring 1 should sit near 3.0 GHz and ring 5 near 6.8 GHz. Both are inside the 2 to 9 GHz band.

## 0.4 Encoding Bits
- **A present ring is a 1, and a missing ring is a 0.**
- To clear a bit, delete that ring from **all four groups**.
- Removing ring 2 left four notches in the simulation, which gives **10111**.

## 0.5 Angle of Incidence
- theta was swept over 0°, 30° and 60°.
- All five notches stay at **exactly the same frequencies**. Only their depth changes as the angle grows.
- So the tag still reads correctly at an angle.

## 0.6 Polarization
- phi was swept over 0° and 90°, and the two RCS results are **identical**.
- So the tag is **polarization independent**. Its layout looks the same after a 90° turn, so a 90° turn of the wave changes nothing.
- This is why [[8. Chipless RFID Fundamentals|Section 8]]'s tag doesn't really give 14 bits: symmetric resonators repeat the same code.

## 0.7 Two Tags Compared
| | Hexagon tag (Section 8) | Square ring tag (this section) |
|---|---|---|
| **Bits** | 7 | 5 |
| **Size** | 22 × 10 mm | 30 × 30 mm |
| **Substrate** | FR-4, 1.6 mm | FR-4, 1.6 mm |
| **Band** | 4 to 20 GHz | 2 to 9 GHz |
| **Groups of rings** | 2 | 4 |
| **At φ = 90°** | Slight change | Identical |
